source_document.body:
This year’s study of the top issues facing trucking undertaken by the American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) had a number one concern that didn’t even crack the top 10 in the prior two years: fuel prices .
That issue was number one in the responses submitted by drivers and number two for carriers, finishing in the top slot overall.
The carriers’ rating is particularly notable, because it undercuts the idea that fuel surcharges are able to effectively move the cost of fuel on to the shipper with little impact on the carrier, or that higher prices and the fuel surcharges that come with are a positive for carriers. The results in the survey suggest otherwise, at least to some degree.
Although fuel prices didn’t make the list the last two years , ATRI, the research arm of the American Trucking Associations (ATA), said 2026 was the fourth time in the 22 years of its top 10 survey that fuel prices were the number one overall concern.
ATRI revealed its top 10 list Sunday at the ATA’s annual Management Conference & Exhibition meeting in Charlotte.
Not since 2023
Prior to appearing again on the ATRI list of “critical concerns in the trucking industry,” which is what the group calls its annual survey, fuel prices were most recently number 3 on the list for drivers in 2023, when diesel at that point had set an all-time record for prices. It was number five on the list that year for carriers. But the issue was nowhere to be found in 2024 and 2025.
The highest average weekly retail diesel price reported by the Energy Information Administration in 2022 was $5.341/g on October 24. While the price was down in 2023, it remained above $4/gallon until May and then climbed back above $5 for most of August into November.
The highest EIA weekly level this year was $6.529 on September 22, which also was the highest in the data series’ history. The AAA’s daily average fuel price hit a record in September as well.
Best practices post-Montgomery
The case of Montgomery vs. Caribe Transport II could be seen in the high rankings for several categories.
For example, motor carrier Compliance Safety Accountability (CSA) scores were fourth in 2025 and fifth this year for motor carriers, third overall.
One observation made by brokers is that in the post-Montgomery world where they are more likely to be held liable in a crash, what constitutes a best practice that in any subsequent litigation they can cite as having proved they did adequate due diligence in hiring a carrier? For example, the nuclear verdict in Lipe vs. Lupus Superior involved a motor carrier with a Satisfactory rating from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration .
FMCSA officials have said they do not view their scores as a ratings tool.
But that did not appear to be acknowledged in the ATRI list of strategies to deal with CSA scores.
“Compliance Safety Accountability – FMCSA’s safety measurement system – has been a top 10 issue for 16 of the 17 years since CSA debuted on the list as the #2 overall concern in 2010,” the ATRI report said. “This year, driven in large part by the SCOTUS ruling, CSA is back up to the industry’s #3 overall concern, its highest ranking since 2015.”
From left to right at the ATA MCE meeting, revealing the ATRI top 10:
Rebecca Brewster, outgoing head of ATRI; Ben Banks, president of TCW;
Jason Damon, Convoy Systems; Gary Johnson, Motive
While the respondents want FMCSA to address “enforcement disparities” and “geographic variations” in its work, there seemed to be little question that the industry believes CSA scores will help them in a lawsuit.
“Based on the (Montgomery) ruling, brokers will need documented evidence that they hired the safest carriers to avoid negligent hiring claims, and carrier CSA scores are one such form of documentation,” the ATRI report on its survey said.
While the two sides of the trucking industry, driver and carrier, may agree on the impact of fuel prices, the divide that shows up regularly in this annual survey by ATRI was present for other issues.
For drivers, parking is big; for carriers, not so much
For example, truck parking, even after various efforts to improve its availability , showed up as number 2 on the list of drivers. For carriers, it wasn’t even in the top 10.
Lawsuit abuse was number two overall for the second consecutive year. It was number one for carriers. It didn’t show up in the top 10 for drivers.
The divide between carriers and drivers was evident elsewhere. Driver shortage was number 3 for carriers, and not on the top 10 list for drivers. Broker issues: number 8 for drivers, not on the carriers list. Detention /delay at customer facilities was number 7 for drivers and didn’t make the top 10 cut for carriers.
Driver compensation between 2023 and 2026 for drivers was first, second, first and third. It popped up as number nine this year on the carriers’ list, but that is the first time in the last four years it has been in the top 10.
The ATRI survey also seeks input on solutions to the issues raised by the respondents. At the top of the list for lawsuit reform were state-level reforms “to cap non-economic and/or punitive damages paid to plaintiffs in truck-involved crashes.”
Another target strategy for fighting lawsuit abuse, according to the survey, would be to push for what are described as “phantom” medical damages.
ATRI described them as payouts that are ordered “by claiming the original billed total for medical care rather than the amount actually paid for medical care. These inflated costs increase verdict and settlement amounts, and several states – including Florida and Georgia – have passed legislation to rein in plaintiff claims for phantom medical damages.”
Third party lawsuit funding
Another target for fixing the issue, according to the ATRI respondents, would be fighting third party litigation funding, where an outside attorney or group of attorneys provides upfront funding to power a lawsuit.
Insurance cost/availability was fourth on the overall list. Commentary on that brought up Montgomery as well.
“The impacts of the SCOTUS ruling in Montgomery v. Caribe are just now starting to be realized but one thing is certain: insurance rates are likely to increase for motor carriers and brokers,” ATRI said.
The top recommendation for dealing with that issue, according to ATRI, would be to develop a “framework” that could possibly lead insurance companies to reduce premiums “when drivers and carriers adopt proven safety technologies.”

Historic mill at Premier gold project Credit: Cambria Gold Mines
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 19, 2026
High-grade drill results at Cambria Gold Mines’ (TSXV: CAMB; US-OTC: CAMVF) Silver Coin bolster its plans to secure ore for the restart next year of the idled Premier mill in northwestern British Columbia.
Hole SC26-2714 cut 8.2 metres grading 98.56 grams gold per tonne from 73.7 metres downhole, including 1 metre at 794 grams, the company reported Monday. Silver Coin lies 5 km north of the mill near Stewart, about 890 km northwest of Vancouver.
“High gold grades over potentially underground bulk mineable widths at the Silver Coin Deposit makes this area a priority for underground development in the spring of 2027,” President and CEO Robert McLeod said in a release.
Securing enough mineable feed is central to Cambria’s plan to revive the 2,500-tonne-per-day plant after insufficient underground material derailed its earlier production ramp-up. The company plans to blend material from Silver Coin and Big Missouri with higher-grade ore from the Premier deposit while it develops Red Mountain. Cambria says $538 million (US$377.3 million) has been spent since 2021.
The assays strengthen Silver Coin’s potential role as an early source of mill feed, Canaccord Genuity said in a Monday research brief.
Shares were little changed at 71¢ around midday Monday in Toronto. Shares have touched 60¢ and $3.50 apiece over the past 12 months. It has a market capitalization of about $300 million.
Grade checks
The headline interval’s estimated true width is about 5.6 metres, or 68% of its drilled length. The included metre of exceptionally high-grade material accounts for much of the overall grade. True widths across the reported intersections range from 68% to 97% of downhole lengths, according to the company.
Hole SC26-2710 returned 4.4 metres grading 22.62 grams from 91.6 metres downhole and a separate 20 metres at 3.75 grams from 123 metres. Monday’s results cover four holes totalling 657 metres, the first assays released from this year’s Silver Coin infill program.
Cambria expects results from more than 14,000 metres of drilling at the deposit over the next several weeks. The assays are to inform an updated resource estimate and feasibility study targeted for the first half of next year. Infill drilling is expected to continue into 2027, with another round of underground drilling planned early next year.
Restart hurdles
Cambria is targeting mill commissioning late next year, followed by a production ramp-up through 2028, according to its Oct. 5 update . The Vancouver-based company adopted its name in February after restructuring under its former Ascot Resources banner.
The revised approach draws on Silver Coin’s mining history. Westmin and Tenajon Resources mined the deposit’s northern portion in the 1990s. Cambria is using operational information from that work to help model the southern extension, where the latest drilling is focused.
Access could come through existing underground workings at Big Missouri, 700 metres north of Silver Coin, or a new portal closer to the mineralized zones, depending on permitting, the company said early this month.
The restart still requires plant upgrades, mine authorizations and work on water treatment. Cambria said earlier this month it was moving closer to meeting zinc discharge limits after equipment upgrades and changes to treatment-plant operations.
At Red Mountain, the company plans to build the alpine section of its access road next year. It ultimately intends to truck material about 50 km to Premier through Stewart and Hyder, Alaska.

source_document.body:
A.P. Moller-Maersk is participating in industry studies examining what would be required for nuclear-powered container ships to make routine port calls , with the work centered on regulation, safety, security and port operations rather than an immediate vessel-ordering program.
The Danish carrier — the world’s second-largest by capacity — (OTC: AMKBY ) joined Lloyd’s Register and reactor developer Core Power in 2024 to assess the regulatory feasibility of operating a containership using a fourth-generation nuclear reactor at a European port. The study focused on a feeder vessel, a smaller containership used to connect regional ports with major hub terminals .
A subsequent case study involving the Port of Rotterdam evaluated calls by a hypothetical 3,600-TEU Maersk feeder vessel. The participants concluded that the core obstacles were largely regulatory and governance-related rather than purely technical, including nuclear-specific port safety procedures, emergency preparedness, physical protection, liability, insurance and coordination between maritime and nuclear authorities.
Maersk has said the work should not be interpreted as a commitment to deploy nuclear propulsion. Instead, the carrier is assessing nuclear energy as one potential long-term zero-emission pathway while identifying the safety, waste-management, legal and public-acceptance issues that would need resolution before commercial operations could be considered.
The inquiry has since expanded beyond Europe. In September, Maersk and Lloyd’s Register announced a conceptual UK-U.S. “Pink Corridor” project involving the ports of Felixstowe and Charleston, S.C. The initiative is intended to study safeguards and security requirements for a potential transatlantic nuclear-powered containership service.
The first phase will consider ship security, nuclear safeguards, cyber resilience, emergency response, insurance and the alignment of maritime and nuclear regulations. Its findings could define a later phase examining engineering, legal, legislative and safeguards requirements in greater detail.
State agency SC Ports said the work gives the hub an opportunity to study a potential nuclear-powered freight corridor, while Lloyd’s Register said the project is intended to establish the practical requirements and gaps that would need to be addressed before such a service could be considered.
The Charleston project arrives amid wider U.S. government interest in commercial maritime nuclear power. The U.S. Department of Energy and classification society ABS signed an agreement to examine nuclear-powered vessels, floating nuclear power applications, and the port, shipyard and industrial infrastructure needed to support them.
Separately, the U.S. Maritime Administration and Core Power have entered a cooperation agreement on maritime-nuclear frameworks for a prospective U.S.-flag fleet. Core Power has said the framework is aimed at accelerating the commercial, industrial and regulatory work needed for potential nuclear-powered merchant vessels.
The Port of Long Beach and Marad recently signed a first-of-its-kind partnership to develop small modular reactors for commercial vessels, port operations and other maritime uses. Bluecore Energy is developing a 10-megawatt floating reactor concept at the port, though no operating reactor or regulatory approval is in place.

source_document.body:
NEW YORK, NY — High-performance computing has reached a new milestone in New York State. New York University (NYU) has announced the deployment of Torch, a supercomputer that serves as the highest-performing academic computational system in New York State and ranks within the top tier of higher education institutions in the United States.
Named after NYU’s logo, the system marks an expansion for the university’s research community. Clocking in at an official 10.79 petaflops on the LINPACK benchmark, Torch delivers a fivefold increase in computational performance compared to NYU’s previous cluster, Greene. By bringing this capacity on-premises, NYU has established a localized computing environment to expand access to hardware for faculty members, researchers, and students.
Accelerating Research via Advanced Architecture
Architected to handle data-heavy workloads and multi-dimensional simulations, Torch utilizes a parallelized, hybrid architecture. To develop the infrastructure, NYU collaborated with HPE and NVIDIA to support the scale of the university’s research operations.
The system’s specifications include:
The AI Engines: Core workloads are powered by more than 500 NVIDIA H200 Tensor Core GPUs . Utilizing HBM3e memory , these GPUs allow NYU researchers to train large language models (LLMs) and execute deep learning tasks.
System Integration: The HPE Cray XD670 cluster was engineered, integrated, and deployed by HPE, leveraging their deployment experience in academic and enterprise supercomputing environments to maximize operational throughput.
By deploying this hardware ecosystem directly to its campus, NYU research teams can shorten the timeline required to convert theoretical formulations into scientific results.
Focus on Sustainable Innovation
NYU’s implementation of Torch balances computational speed with environmental considerations. Operating with the capacity to process over 10 quadrillion calculations per second , Torch entered the global computing index ranked No. 40 on the Green500 list of energy-efficient supercomputers.
To achieve this level of efficiency, the system utilizes liquid cooling technology designed to dissipate heat at the component level. This minimizes the data center’s reliance on traditional air conditioning methods. The resulting energy profile aligns with NYU’s institutional goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2040 .
NYU leadership indicated that Torch balances academic computing power with energy efficiency. University officials noted it will support research across artificial intelligence, climate modeling, and biomedical sciences while contributing to international collaborations like the Global AI Frontier Lab .
Contextualizing the Fivefold Performance Leap
To understand the impact of Torch, let’s look at the capabilities of its predecessor, the Greene cluster. Greene provided approximately 4 quadrillion calculations per second . While Greene was considered a significant asset for the university—initially ranking No. 50 on the Green500 list—the exponential growth of machine learning, quantum mechanics simulations, and neural network training required an upgrade.
Greene relied on an array of 332 NVIDIA GPUs . While this configuration was optimized for general high-performance computing, it faced operational constraints when tasked with modern large language models containing hundreds of billions of parameters.
Torch alters this baseline. By incorporating NVIDIA H200 Tensor Core GPUs, the network handles matrix multiplications at speeds previously unattainable on campus. The inclusion of high-throughput host processing architecture prevents data delivery lag, so the execution pipelines of the GPUs are continuously supplied with data. The total computing capacity of Torch allows it to clear processing jobs that previously took weeks on the Greene cluster in a fraction of the time .
Eliminating Bottlenecks in the Research Pipeline
In academic computing environments, time-to-results is a critical metric. Previously, universities lacking on-premise infrastructure had to bid for compute time allocations at national laboratories, or rely on public cloud providers. Public cloud alternatives often introduce recurring operational costs, data egress fees, and privacy constraints that complicate institutional research grants.
By building an on-premise infrastructure, NYU changes how its departments handle active projects. Researchers can test models locally, debug network configurations instantly, and run continuous cycles without waiting in queues. This shift benefits fields like:
Artificial Intelligence and Embodied Intelligence: Training transformers and computer vision systems for real-world robotics applications.
Climate Modeling: Simulating localized weather patterns, oceanic heat distribution, and long-term carbon variations at a granular scale.
Biomedical Sciences: Accelerating protein folding computations, gene sequencing analysis, and molecular dynamics modeling for Alzheimer’s disease research.
Engineering for Sustainable Infrastructure
A core issue with data centers housing top-tier AI hardware is energy consumption. NVIDIA H200 GPUs demand significant power, which generates substantial thermal output. Without changes in environmental engineering, a cluster of this size would require massive, power-intensive traditional HVAC configurations.
Torch manages this footprint by integrating its technical deployment with modern environmental design. The cluster utilizes a liquid cooling design where coolant is distributed directly to the processors and memory components. This method removes heat more efficiently than air-based systems, lowering the overall Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) ratio of the facility.
This focus on efficiency allowed Torch to achieve its No. 40 ranking on the global Green500 index. This deployment supports the university’s initiative to minimize its overall environmental footprint, proving that academic research capacity can scale while remaining aligned with a carbon-neutral objective.
Long-Term Institutional Impact
The deployment of Torch is designed to establish NYU as a center for computational science. In higher education, access to computing resources is a differentiator for attractions like faculty, post-doctoral researchers, and graduate students.
Beyond hardware availability, the university intends to integrate Torch into its academic curricula. Graduate and undergraduate students working in data science, physics, engineering, and digital humanities will receive direct training on high-performance computing clusters. This provides students with hands-on experience using hardware configurations identical to those found in global research laboratories and advanced technology enterprises.
As part of its international strategy, Torch will act as the foundational computing engine behind the Global AI Frontier initiative. This network connects NYU’s campuses and global partners, facilitating multi-institutional research on global problems. With Torch operational, the university has established the technical infrastructure required to support data science developments for the coming decade.
Watch the Video Interview
To learn more about the technical architecture and engineering choices behind this system, watch the full video segment. Check out the HPE Video Interview with NYU’s Leadership Team to see how this on-premise hardware ecosystem is actively shrinking the time to science, and visit hpe.com to explore their full portfolio of enterprise and academic AI infrastructure.

Ford Transit Connect Recalled Again Over Rearview Cameras That Still Don't Work
6 photos
Photo: Ford
The Ford Motor Company is pulling 506 vans back into dealerships because the rearview cameras installed under a previous campaign do not do the job as intended. As it happens, the replacement cameras are an older revision that never contained the fix at all.
During the launch of the remedy for safety recall 25V572, a transcription error listed the recalled camera assembly as the remedy part. The dealer bulletin should have said the fix wasn't available yet. Given the aforementioned, service centers ordered what the paperwork named rather than rearview cameras that actually work as intended.
The camera itself is produced by Magna, and there are a few problems with it. From distorted to inverted images and intermittent to persistent loss of image, said design does not meet the federal requirements for rearview cameras. The safety risk that justified the original campaign is still there, unaddressed, in all 506 vans.
Said US-market population comes from warranty claims on vans repaired under the previous recall. FoMoCo identified the problem reasonably fast. The Critical Concerns Review Group started investigating the matter in June 2026, with engineers spending the summer chasing down which vans had been serviced under the wrong instructions.
By September 21, they had the final tally for the United States market. The safety boffins further confirmed no accidents or injuries potentially related to the recall condition. As per the recall documentation, the driver gets no warning before the image misbehaves.
Photo: Ford Production dates for the subject vehicles range from August 1, 2014, through July 28, 2015. Despite being North American vans, they were sourced from the Valencia plant in Spain rather than North America. The Ford Motor Company decided on Spain because the Transit Connect was originally designed for Europe, where compact vans are highly popular.
Ford claims that affected VINs became searchable on the NHTSA's portal back on October 7, 2026. The fix is understandably free, and just like before, a camera swap is on the menu. On this occasion, however, the replacement assemblies will be produced under an updated process with a greater focus on quality control.
Customers who already paid a Ford service center out of pocket have a route back too, since FoMoCo runs a general reimbursement plan for safety recall work. Remedy letters are planned to land no later than December 17, 2027, which indicates that replacement cameras are not readily available at dealers nationwide.
The Ford Motor Company ended sales of the Transit Connect in North America after the 2023 model year, citing poor demand for compact and small vans in this part of the world. Had sales been a little better, Ford may have gone through with a next-gen model that was expected to be produced in Mexico.

source_document.body:
The European Commission approved Germany’s financial support after assessing the risks of Sanofi stopping insulin API production at the Frankfurt campus.
Sanofi has broken ground on an insulin ingredient manufacturing facility in Frankfurt, Germany, weeks after securing €400 million ($449 million) in support from the German government.
The 36,000-square-meter facility is scheduled to start full production of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) in 2032, once the plant is fully licensed. Paris-based Sanofi is building the facility at its Frankfurt site, which already handles API manufacturing, filling, device assembly and packaging for about 20 insulin products. Sanofi employs around 4,000 people dedicated to insulin at the site.
While Sanofi committed to building an insulin ingredient production plant in Frankfurt in August 2024, the company was set to close its API manufacturing facility unless the German government provided financial support, the European Commission said last month when approving the aid.
The German government offered Sanofi €400 million ($449 million) to compensate for the costs involved in making the insulin supply chain more resilient. Under European Union rules, Germany needed the Commission’s approval to provide the support.
In return for the funding, Sanofi has committed to building a new insulin factory in Frankfurt by the end of 2032 and ensuring annual production of at least 1.1 metric tons of insulin until the end of 2042. The Commission also required Sanofi to stockpile a metric ton of insulin API until the end of 2042 and to prioritize the European Economic Area (EEA) during insulin shortages.
The approval of the financial support reflects concerns about how the threatened closure of the facility would impact European patients. If Sanofi shuttered the API plant, the EEA would only have one insulin production facility. Novo makes about half the world’s insulin from a site in Denmark.
Without the Sanofi plant, the EU would be more reliant on overseas insulin imports, the Commission said. Officials added that insulin supply shortages have become more frequent as production capacity is diverted to GLP-1 receptor agonists.
Sanofi broke ground on the API facility weeks after the Commission approved the state aid, providing momentum for a construction project first disclosed more than two years ago. Back then, Sanofi outlined plans to invest €1.3 billion ($1.5 billion) and open the insulin API facility by 2029.
The European project has advanced in parallel to Sanofi’s addition of insulin manufacturing capacity in China. The French drugmaker committed €1 billion ($1.1 billion) to build an insulin manufacturing plant in Beijing in December 2024. The company broke ground on the facility in October 2025.

EyePoint is initiating a strategic review after duravyu failed another Phase 3 trial in wet age-related macular degeneration. Amid significant layoffs and trial terminations, the company is shifting attention to the asset’s potential in diabetic macular edema.
Following another disappointing readout for investigational tyrosine kinase inhibitor duravyu in wet age-related macular degeneration, EyePoint will undergo a strategic reprioritization that includes cutting about 53% of its workforce.
On Monday, EyePoint reported that in the topline readout from the Phase 3 Lucia trial, duravyu again failed to match Regeneron Pharmaceuticals’ approved wet AMD treatment Eylea. The Watertown, Massachusetts–based biotech is now ending the asset’s pivotal wet AMD trials early, the company said in a separate Monday announcement , and will focus resources on its late-stage program for duravyu in diabetic macular edema (DME).
EyePoint had 214 employees as of Feb. 27, according to an annual report , meaning the layoffs could affect 113 people.
Following the news, the biotech’s stock plummeted more than 80% at market open to 55 cents per share.
EyePoint first signaled problems for duravyu in August. In the Phase 3 Lugano trial, the candidate failed to meet the study’s primary endpoint of improving average change in vision after two years as compared to Eylea or an Eylea biosimilar—the current standard of care for wet AMD.
Monday’s readout showed that the Lucia trial had a similar outcome. Duravyu failed to meet its primary endpoint of statistical non-inferiority in mean change in best corrected visual acuity. The candidate did, however, meet key secondary endpoints, including superior reduction in treatment burden.
EyePoint plans to complete additional analyses of Lucia and pooled Phase 3 datasets to determine next steps for the candidate as a wet AMD treatment but is ending both pivotal trials early without completing a second year.

As to duravyu in DME, the company expects a pivotal Phase 3 readout for two trials during the fourth quarter. In the biotech’s announcement about the strategic reprioritization, President and CEO Jay Duker noted that the company is evaluating duravyu’s potential to offer a durable, long-term therapeutic option that safely reduces the overall injection burden for patients.
EyePoint expects most of its workforce reduction will take place during the fourth quarter and will be completed in the first half of 2027. The company estimates it will incur aggregate charges of about $9 million related to employee separation benefits.

Mexico's 2027 Chevrolet Trax Crossover Gets More Than Merely a New Grille
11 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
Chevrolet's refreshed Trax has been confirmed for Mexico, where it will reach dealers between April 2027 and June 2027 for the 2027 model year. Among the most interesting updates of the facelift is the optional power liftgate, which Chevy describes as a first for the front-biased crossover.
The new grille is dandy and all, but a hatch that opens electrically is the more pragmatic update when your hands are full of groceries and other whatnots. More substantial work hides behind the skin, for General Motors has changed the electrical and software architectures to enable a wider collection of safety systems and Google-powered infotainment.
A pretty big undertaking for a facelift, giving the 2027 model a stronger argument than a different color palette and fresh wheels. Chevrolet further lists rear cross-traffic braking and reverse automatic braking, alongside front and rear parking assistance for good measure. There's also blind-spot steering assistance, side bicyclist alert, and adaptive cruise control.
Intersection emergency braking also made the cut, as did the safety alert seat feature. As you might have already guessed, the latter is designed to vibrate the driver's seat cushion rather than depending solely on a chime to warn about potential crash risks. The safety alert seat vibrates in directional pulses, showing the driver where the hazard is coming from.
Gifted with a revised grille that makes the Trax more assertive than before, the 2027 model further adds new wheel designs and LED exterior lighting. The ACTIV grade illustrates the most outdoorsy specification available for Mexico, dedicated front-end styling and all.
Photo: Chevrolet The RS grade takes the sporty-looking route with large wheels, whereas the entry version uses a higher-contrast wheel finish for a more urban appearance. Alas, front-wheel drive remains the norm because the Trax and the platform were developed with low costs, high efficiency, and interior space in mind. The lack of all-wheel drive also means the Trax doesn't compete with the Trailblazer.
An 11-inch digital instrument cluster sits alongside a similarly sized infotainment touchscreen, and the dash is further beautified by hexagonal outer vents. Speaking of the interior, Storm Sky Gray introduced an earthier theme. Google built-in goodies need highlighting as well, complete with Gemini assistance.
While connectivity details for Mexico remain to be determined, it's worth remembering that Chevrolet has already confirmed wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for the United States of America. OnStar's revised offering includes a hotspot that can connect up to seven devices, plus video streaming capability.
Under the hood, you will find a puny three-pot turbo with 137 horsepower and 162 pound-feet (220 Newton-meters) to its name. A six-speed automatic is standard, and the number of forward ratios also demonstrates that General Motors developed a cost-centric crossover here. Just like the US model, the Mexican Trax should arrive in base, RS, and ACTIV flavors in the second quarter of 2027.

According to Nikkei, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.
The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrain options.
Toyota Corolla Concept (Source: Toyota)
Adapt or fall behind
Toyota already uses the platform for several models, including under its luxury Lexus brand. By building the new Corolla in China, Toyota is expected to cut costs while speeding up development and output.
In addition to new longer-range electric vehicles, Toyota plans to build extended-range EVs under Lexus in China starting next year.
Toyota has yet to reveal any battery, powertrain specs, or other details. The next-gen Corolla is expected to remain close to the concept with a sleek, almost sports-car-like design. Aside from the huge COROLLA badge on the rear, you can barely tell it’s a Corolla.
Toyota CEO Koji Sato reveals the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show (Source: Toyota)
In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company is being forced to adapt, or “it cannot survive,” amid new competition and technology from China.
The special broadcast went behind the scenes at the “top secret” next-gen Corolla development site.
During the broadcast, several Corolla Concept body types , including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were shown blurred in the background.
Toyota Corolla Concept (Source: Toyota)
The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.
The hybrid will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.
Whether or not Toyota will bring the Corolla EV to the US is still unclear. Toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year.
According to Car and Driver , the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.
Electrek’s Take
While the Corolla is still a top seller, it has lost some of its charm as newer vehicles arrive that are more advanced, more efficient, and better looking.
It’s about time for an overhaul. In China, Toyota’s sales dropped by 23%, marking the seventh straight month of lower sales due to weak demand for gas and hybrid models amid soaring fuel prices.
Toyota is restructuring its two joint ventures , FAW Toyota and GAC Toyota, to streamline operations and introduce more advanced tech in China.

The Defense Department has signed a framework agreement with BAE Systems to buy up to 25,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System, or APKWS, guidance kits a year for as long as seven years, the department announced Monday .
APKWS kits convert unguided 2.75-inch rockets into laser-guided munitions. All four services field them, and the weapon has become a cheaper alternative to air-to-air missiles for shooting down drones.
Congress still has to approve and fund the buy, the department said. BAE said it will increase production while the two sides work out a multiyear contract. Neither side announced the deal’s cost.
The framework also outlines a path to increase output to 35,000 kits a year for U.S. allies. The department said that added capacity will come online as partner nations formally request kits through the Foreign Military Sales program.
“By securing multi-year demand, this agreement keeps production lines running at capacity, provides our forces with interceptor inventory, and flips the cost calculus in the taxpayer’s favor,” Michael Duffey, the Pentagon’s undersecretary for acquisition and sustainment, said in the announcement.
BAE, which builds the kits in Hudson, New Hampshire, and Austin, Texas, said in February that it had delivered its 100,000th kit .
The 25,000 figure in this framework agreement matches capacity BAE has cited before. A company official said in 2023 that APKWS was in full-rate production with room to grow to 25,000 units a year.
“APKWS delivers proven, reliable and affordable precision at scale to counter evolving threats and ensure our warfighters maintain a decisive advantage,” said Tom Arseneault, president and CEO of BAE Systems Inc.
The Navy’s current five-year APKWS contract with BAE, awarded in August 2025 , is worth up to $1.74 billion. It covers up to 55,000 kits for the Navy, the Army and foreign customers, with work expected to be completed by December 2031.
Among allied buyers, Saudi Arabia won State Department approval in July for a possible $1.96 billion package that includes up to 20,000 APKWS kits, split evenly between air-to-air and air-to-ground versions. Italy is also weighing a buy of 5,031 kits for counter-drone defense.
The APKWS agreement is the latest in a series of framework deals the Pentagon has signed this year to boost munitions production.
In January, Lockheed Martin agreed to more than triple production of the Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement, or PAC-3 MSE, interceptor.
In March, BAE and Lockheed agreed to quadruple production of seekers for the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense, or THAAD, interceptor. A separate THAAD framework signed in January led to a June contract worth more than $35 billion for the interceptors themselves.

By: Henry Lazenby October 19, 2026
Military Metals (CSE: MILI; US-OTC: MILIF) secured four more years to explore its Trojárová antimony-gold project in Slovakia after authorities reversed a decision to cancel its licence. Shares rose.
The exploration permit now runs to Oct. 18, 2030, the Vancouver-based company said Monday. The project lies near Pezinok, about 20 km northeast of the capital, Bratislava.
“Europe has significant antimony supply-chain exposure because it lacks meaningful domestic mine production and depends heavily on external suppliers for its raw-material needs,” CEO Scott Eldridge said in a release.
The reprieve restores the company’s ability to advance a potential European source of a metal used in ammunition, flame retardants and electronics. Turning that resource into supply still requires mining and production approvals, with technical, environmental and community work ahead.
Company shares jumped 28% to 25.5¢ apiece on Monday, after testing 15¢ and 56¢ apiece over the past 12 months. It has a market capitalization of $20.5 million (US$14.5 million).
Licence reversal
The May licence cancellation was overturned because the decision was unlawful, Slovakia’s Environment Ministry said Monday. The ministry confirmed the licence holder met all conditions for a four-year exploration extension, while stressing that future mining would require environmental assessment and separate approvals.
The cancellation followed an unscheduled review on May 28. Military Metals challenged the decision, filing an appeal on June 12 and arguing the cancellation was unjustified.
The company argued the cancellation conflicted with the ministry’s inclusion of Trojárová in Slovakia’s national critical-minerals exploration program submitted to the European Commission. That designation identified the site as an exploration area for antimony, the company said in its appeal announcement.
Trojárová holds 6.5 million inferred tonnes grading 1.02% antimony and 1.06 grams gold per tonne, containing about 67,000 tonnes of antimony and 222,000 oz. gold, according to SLR Consulting’s estimate effective April 6.
Development path
Military Metals has begun discussions with Slovak authorities and the Economy Ministry on the requirements for mining and production authorization. Monday’s announcement didn’t set a construction or production timetable.
The company plans to establish a local advisory board to engage neighbouring communities and authorities on environmental priorities and development. It also intends to work with specialists on local wastewater management and expand cooperation with the Technical University of Košice on mineral processing and water research.
The April resource estimate replaced historical figures derived from exploration during the communist era. SLR incorporated 53 diamond drill holes totalling 7,167 metres and 202 metres of underground chip sampling into the estimate, which Military Metals supported with confirmation drilling completed last year.

1971 Dodge Super Bee Barn Find Emerges With Rare Factory Feature
17 photos
Photo: Craiglist
In 1966, Dodge debuted the first-generation Charger , the first Hemi-powered Mopar. The Charger was the brand's second B-body intermediate, joining the Coronet. Two years later, Dodge added a third model to the lineup, the Super Bee. The company's affordable muscle car, it debuted alongside the Plymouth Road Runner.
While the latter was quite successful, moving over 120,000 units in its first two years on the market, the Super Bee moved significantly fewer cars. Sales peaked at 27,800 units in 1969, but Dodge delivered only 56,202 examples between 1968 and 1971. The final-year version is the rarest of the bunch, with only 5,054 made.
Like most golden-era Mopars, the 1971 Super Bee is the most sought-after in its Hemi configuration. This one is also rare, with only 22 produced. The 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) V8 vehicles are also scarce. Dodge sold only 26 equipped with the four-barrel mill and just 99 with the Six-Pack setup.
The 340-cubic-inch (5.6-liter) small-block V8, which was offered for the first time in the Super Bee in 1971, found its way into only 307 examples. This leaves us with 3,858 cars equipped with the standard 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8 engine.
These Super Bees aren't particularly desirable, especially when they re-emerge into the light after decades of improper storage. The red example you see here is one of those 383-equipped models, but it's also rare thanks to a drivetrain component you don't see very often. I'm talking about the transmission.
Most 383-equipped Super Bees were born with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic; records indicate 2,889 units. The four-speed manual version is notably rarer, as only 766 were ordered with the three-pedal layout. Well, this Mopar doesn't have that either; the original owner went with the basic configuration by pairing the 383-cubic-inch V8 with the three-speed manual transmission.
The latter was standard with the said powerplant, but most customers opted to upgrade to the four-speed or the TorqueFlite. Apparently, this Super Bee is one of only 203 examples ordered with this drivetrain combo. It's also one of far fewer units that are still around. The 1971 Super Bee Registry, which includes about 750 cars, lists only 18 vehicles with the three-speed automatic. This one would be the 19th.
The Mopar surfaced in Talladega, Alabama, and it looks like it has been off the road for a very long time. There's not much info to run by, but it was probably retired decades ago. Fortunately, the coupe is still in one piece, with not much rust to write home about. The paint could be original, but it's heavily weathered.
The interior appears to be complete, and it's actually in pretty good shape, but it needs a thorough cleaning. The floor pans need some work, as does the trunk pan. The car is missing the hood, and the right-side front fender is a bit crusty.
Sadly, the original engine is missing, with no info on what might have happened. The good news is that 383-cubic-inch V8s aren't difficult to source, with plenty of period-correct units likely out there. But the best news in this department is that the three-speed manual is still with the car. It's sitting in the trunk for now, but it can be restored.
The seller says that the Super Bee has two fender tags, indicating that it's probably a highly optioned car. Unfortunately, he did not include images of the plates, so the options list remains a mystery.
All told, this Super Bee is a pretty solid project car that will morph into a rare collectible. Not quite as desirable as a Hemi, but rare nevertheless. If you've been looking for a three-speed manual Mopar, this Super Bee is available for $12,500 .

I Interviewed Irvin Zonca, Assetto Corsa Rally’s Game Director: We’re in Good Hands!
35 photos
Photo: Irvin Zonca
I’ve been visiting various parts of Greece for almost two decades now. It’s one of my favorite countries in the world, alongside Japan. I’ve always been fascinated by its ancient stories, regardless if we’re talking about mythology or actual history. And for 16+ years now, I’ve fallen in love with its cuisine as well.
One of the dishes that drives me crazy is called “Soutzoukakia”, and I’ve learned how to cook it at home. Discovering its ingredients one by one, and getting used to the right method of bringing them together wasn’t enough for me. I wanted to know who invented it, and for how long it has been part of Greece’s culinary history. Long story short, it arrived from the Turkish region of Smyrna, which used to be a Greek settlement before a refugee crisis changed the region forever (along with its name- Izmir).
You migh ask what all of this has to do with the conversation I had recently with Irvin Zonca, the Creative and Game Director for Assetto Corsa Rally. The fact that the Akropolis Rally Greece is one of the events I like driving the most in the game (alongside Monte Carlo) isn’t the only explanation. Supernova’s project has had such a profound impact on me that I didn’t just want to settle with playing the game. I needed to know more about its development and the people behind it.
It has been obvious since day one that they are passionate about the sport, otherwise we would’ve ended up with a title like – I won’t name any names here, but you can instantly tell when a developer only cares about making money and not providing an authentic gameplay experience. Still, I wanted to “double-check” by talking to some at Supernova about AC Rally , and Irvin was kind enough to provide some answers.
He’s a few years older than me, and was born in Borgomanero, Italy, which is also the birthplace of two-time Italian Rally Champion Piero Longhi. “I grew up during the years when the Lancia Delta was dominating the world of rallying, and Senna was racing in Formula 1. I started watching rallies as a teenager, going with friends and sleeping in tents so we could watch the night stages. Several times a year, I would also go to Maggiora to watch the Autocross Championship".
We will be introducing another Group B car Photo: Irvin Zonca/Supernova Games Studios "So, I was surrounded by the racing world, while on the other hand, I was also playing a huge number of video games. I fell in love with driving simulations in the ’90s, with games such as Crammond’s GP2 and GP Legends, as well as all the early rally simulations on PC, while also enjoying arcade and console games. In 2005, at the age of 21, I joined Milestone and worked on around forty racing games, both motorcycle and car titles, gaining experience with MotoGP , SBK, WRC, Supercross and MXGP."
"In 2021, I had the opportunity to join the Digital Bros group and fulfill one of my dreams: working on the Assetto Corsa brand by developing a spin-off dedicated to rallying” . I’m sure every AC Rally enthusiast is eager to know when the next updates are coming, and what cars and rallies they’ll bring with them. “Our plan is to release an update approximately every two months, or at most every two and a half months in exceptional circumstances when the amount of work involved in an update is particularly large."
"Unfortunately, I can’t give you any more details, but I can tell you that over the coming months we will be introducing another Group B car, along with a very special variant of it, as well as more Group A cars. We are also working on two new rallies that are diametrically opposed to each other.” Let’s analyze that for a moment. Update 0.6 arrived in September, which means we might get lucky with more content in November.
I know this could just be wishful thinking, but one of the photos Irvin sent me featured the Lancia Delta S4. If that’s an accurate guess, could it mean the very special variant is the road-going version? Also, the only Group B car we’ve had in the game so far was the Lancia Rally 037 EVO 2 (1984), so there’s certainly plenty of room for interpretation. I also asked about maybe having a Suggestion Box for the future, as it could potentially provide the team with a wide selection of useful ideas.
There are many rally enthusiasts on the team Photo: Irvin Zonca/Supernova Games Studios I guess I might be getting old here, as I had forgotten about Assetto Corsa’s Discord channel, which is constantly monitored by the team. “The community has welcomed and supported the project from the very beginning, understanding and embracing our “quality over quantity” philosophy. We are very grateful to them, and we promise that we will continue working hard to give them the best rally simulator we are capable of developing. Especially because we are the first ones who want to play it ourselves!”
When I tested Update 0.4 back in April, I discovered how fun Colin McRae’s Subaru Impreza S3 Group A was, and also that one of the game’s sound designers was an Impreza owner himself. I know how demanding I am with analyzing how RX-7s sound in video games, and I imagine Mr. Mark ‘TDK’ Knight is even more so given that this is part of job. But what else do we know about some of the other people working on Assetto Corsa Rally?
“There are many other rally enthusiasts on the team, and we have shared some wonderful days visiting collections, recording rally cars, or watching real rallies together. In particular, with our handling designer, Giuseppe “Abbo90”, we have taken part in several driving courses, both on ice and gravel, driving cars such as Mitsubishi Lancers, Subaru Imprezas and a Group 2 Ford Escort. Other members of the team are sim racers, and some are also content creators, such as Matt, who runs the “Yorkie065” channel."
"This is why we are able to focus on the details that enthusiasts are really looking for: we are the first ones to be genuinely passionate about rallying ourselves. As for collaborations, we work with several real-world drivers, including Jon Armstrong, a Ford M-Sport driver who is currently competing in the World Rally Championship. Jon is an exceptional guy with tremendous talent both in the real world and on simulators, and he is helping us enormously with the evolution of the game’s physics."
We ourselves have spent a lot of time playing both games Photo: autoevolution "We also collaborate with people such as Tommaso Ciuffi and Ike Racing, which competes in the European Historic Rally Championship.” Just as some people might try to compare Max Versappen to Ayrton Senna, or Marc Marquez to Valentino Rossi, some rally enthusiasts out there might have something to say about their all-time favorite video game: Richard Burns Rally. I haven’t played it myself (I spent some time with DiRT Rally), but it sure is regarded as one of the greatest titles ever made.
I wanted to know how Irvin and the team feel about these comparisons, and if they ever try to learn from the successes and failures of projects that came before theirs. “I come from the sim racing world and have always played as many titles as possible, finding something to appreciate in each of them. As for ACR, we ourselves have spent a lot of time playing both games, so I think it’s a positive thing that our fans do the same. The feedback we receive helps us continue moving in the right direction."
"RBR was considered the best rally simulator for a long time, while DiRT Rally is an example of the incredible talent that existed at Codemasters during those years. With ACR, we want to create a simulator that is realistic, fun, and complete in terms of features, so that it can remain a benchmark both today and in the future. ACR is still in Early Access, which means it is not yet in its final form."
"In our vision, beyond adding content such as stages and cars, there is a continuous evolution of the driving model, as well as the addition of new game modes and online and offline features, including VR. ACR will be supported for years and will continue to grow and improve.” I spent dozens of hours going up Pikes Peak in DiRT Rally, and am currently disappointed Polyphony won’t add the Race to the Clouds in GT7 . Even if it does happen, they’ll likely go for the tarmac setup which isn’t what I’m hoping for.
I’m under strict order not to say too much Photo: autoevolution Sadly, it doesn’t seem to be on table for the team at Supernova for now either. Chances are iconic cars that competed at Pikes Peak won’t be part of the roster any time soon, even though Irvin mentioned they could license something like the Escudo from Suzuki directly. Priority Bicycles has spent the last decade proving that bicycles don’t need to be complicated to be good. Now the New York-based bicycle company is taking one of its more playful pedal bikes and giving it the electric treatment with the new Priority E-Sauce .
The E-Sauce is based on Priority’s existing Sauce, a chunky-tired, belt-driven, single-speed bicycle that was originally expected to appeal to a fairly narrow group of riders. (Fun fact: it also comes in an 8-speed internally geared hub variant, known as the Hot Sauce.)
Instead of living out its product life in obscurity as a bike between niches, Priority says the bike found a much wider audience than they originally expected thanks to its relaxed riding style, distinctive looks, and ability to handle everything from city streets to trails.
And so, naturally, now they stuck a motor on it.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Unlike many of the e-bike companies we cover, Priority didn’t spring up during the e-bike boom with a catalog of imported electric bicycles. The Manhattan-based company was founded by legit cyclists and spent years building traditional bicycles before increasingly embracing electrification. Its calling card has long been bike-shop-quality construction paired with unusually low-maintenance components, particularly Gates carbon belt drives, which the company features on every model it offers, right down to their cute little kids’ bikes .
That same formula carries over to the E-Sauce, which uses a single-speed Gates belt drive rather than a derailleur and chain. Power comes from a 750W rear hub motor, and there’s a throttle for riders who don’t feel like pedaling. The bike ships configured as Class 2 with a 20 mph (32 km/h) speed limit, though pedal assist can be unlocked for speeds of up to 28 mph (45 km/h).
Be sure to check your local regulations to see how that impacts where you can ride. In most states though, the bike will be a 100% street-legal Class 2 e-bike.
Interestingly, Priority is using both torque and cadence sensing – a move we’re starting to see more of.
The torque sensor provides more natural-feeling pedal assist up to 20 mph, while the bike can switch over to cadence-based assistance above 20 mph, meaning they don’t have to pedal like crazy to still get good motor output at higher speeds.
That gives riders the more bicycle-like response of a torque sensor at typical riding speeds without making it difficult to keep the motor working as the bike approaches its 28 mph maximum.
Remember, of course, that the bike only ships in 20 mph mode, and so this will only affect riders who do choose to open it up for more speed to reach the Class 3 limit of 28 mph.
The rest of the bike leans into the Sauce’s do-anything personality. There are wide 27.5 x 2.4-inch WTB Intersector tires and 100mm of front suspension travel, giving it considerably more capability on rough roads and light trails than your typical commuter.
Priority also seems intent on making the E-Sauce surprisingly useful as a utility bike. Standard rear rack mounts work with conventional racks, including Priority’s MIK-compatible rack for carrying panniers, cargo, or even a child seat. Up front, the company’s new frame-mounted Headway Mount will support front racks and other accessories. The bike includes built-in LED lighting, but offers clever innovations like seat-tube integration for the tail light so you don’t have to worry about a light getting whacked off at a crowded bike rack.
Priced at $2,199 , the E-Sauce obviously isn’t going to win a watt-per-dollar battle against the endless sea of $1,000-ish 750W e-bikes. But that’s also missing the point. The E-Sauce is a different type of product. You’re getting a belt-driven bike designed around nearly zero maintenance, built by an actual bicycle company run by real bike people, yet still sold with the convenience and pricing advantages of a direct-to-consumer model.
Priority says that simplicity is central to the bike: a smooth and quiet Gates belt drive, punchy hydraulic disc brakes, quality components, minimal upkeep, and enough versatility to serve as anything from a trail toy to a commuter or light-duty cargo bike.
The original Sauce apparently taught Priority that a fun, simple bicycle can have a much broader audience than expected. With a 750W motor and throttle now thrown into the mix, I have a feeling the E-Sauce might cast an even wider net.

Shippers moving cargo from Asia to North America face tighter vessel capacity and greater difficulty securing bookings in the weeks ahead, while deteriorating service reliability threatens delivery schedules across major east-west trades, according to WiseTech Global’s October Ocean Freight Risk Outlook.
Capacity remains comparatively plentiful on Asia-Europe and Europe-North America routes, but available slots do not necessarily translate into on-time arrivals. On the trans-Pacific, reduced planned carrier capacity is expected to compound already weak service performance .
“Capacity is forecast to tighten towards the end of the outlook period, driven by reduced planned carrier capacity rather than stronger demand,” WiseTech said of the Asia-North America trade. Its booking security risk indicator also is expected to rise and remain well above its historical average, signaling greater difficulty obtaining space on preferred sailings.
The four-week outlook combines forecast demand, planned carrier supply, booking responses, shipment arrival performance and port operating conditions. Its reliability measure tracks the share of shipments arriving at the discharge port on or before the carrier’s promised schedule.
Trans-Pacific faces booking and delivery pressure
Asia-North America on-time performance fell to 26.9% in September from 33.9% in August, a decline of 7 percentage points. The latest weekly reading was little better at 26.8%, while delays of eight days or more remained the largest arrival-outcome category.
WiseTech attributed increased waterside operating pressure in September to continuing disruption at Asian ports, with vessel delays reducing effective trans-Pacific capacity. China’s Golden Week holiday adds disruption to production and cargo flows, meaning a subsequent easing in demand may not immediately improve booking availability or schedule reliability, the report said.
Published schedules nevertheless show relatively short transit times. Planned Asia-North America transits range from 26.2 to 27.6 days during the outlook period, below the recent 28-day baseline. WiseTech cautioned that weak actual performance continues to create uncertainty around arrival dates despite those scheduled transit times.
The company advised forwarders and beneficial cargo owners to book early against contracted allocations and build additional time into delivery commitments, taking individual carriers’ reliability into account. Its analysis found substantial differences in service performance and booking acceptance risk among the trade’s top 10 carriers.
Asia-Europe reliability falls below 10%
The sharpest deterioration in monthly on-time performance occurred on Asia-Europe services, where the September reading fell to 9.9% from 22.9% in August. The latest weekly result improved modestly to 11.5%, but shipments delayed eight days or more accounted for 45.5% of volume that week.
Unlike the trans-Pacific, Asia-Europe is not expected to face a lane-wide capacity constraint during the forecast period. Planned carrier supply remains above projected demand, while booking security risk stays well below its historical average. Some tightening is expected late in the period as carriers reduce planned capacity, rather than because demand strengthens.
That leaves delivery execution, rather than securing vessel space, as the principal concern.
“Shorter published schedules do not indicate improved service reliability, with recent arrival performance continuing to show substantial delays,” WiseTech said. Planned transit times range from 37.8 to 39.9 days, below the recent 40.7-day baseline.
The report pointed to Asian port congestion and changes between Suez Canal-Red Sea and diverted Mideast routings around Africa as possible contributors to broader network disruption. Even the stronger-performing carriers have weak recent on-time results, limiting the protection that carrier selection alone can provide against shipment delays, WiseTech said.
Trans-Atlantic space remains available
Europe-North America presents a comparatively less constrained capacity outlook, with planned supply exceeding forecast demand throughout the period and booking security risk generally easing below its historical average. Increased planned capacity and softer demand initially improve conditions, followed by some tightening as planned capacity declines later in the outlook.
Reliability nevertheless weakened. Monthly on-time performance slipped to 39.2% in September from 42.8% in August. The latest weekly reading improved to 38.6%, with on-time arrivals representing the largest outcome category.
Carrier choice could make a substantial difference on the route: September on-time performance ranged from approximately 14% to 61% among carriers, according to WiseTech. Scheduled transit times remain broadly around the recent 19.1-day baseline, ranging from 17.7 to 19.5 days.

source_document.body:
Supercomputers often feel like distant, abstract machines housed in secure federal facilities. However, one of the world’s most powerful supercomputer, El Capitan at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) , is actively reshaping human safety, medicine, and energy. Behind its mind-boggling speed are real-world applications that directly protect your family, your health, and your planet.
Instant Tsunami Warnings for Coastal Communities
For anyone living near or visiting a coastline, an undersea earthquake starts a terrifying countdown. Traditional emergency models take minutes or hours to calculate wave impact, often leading to delayed warnings or costly false alarms.
Using El Capitan, scientists created a real-time tsunami “digital twin.” This framework connects ocean sensors with physics-based models to calculate precise, hyper-localized coastal risks in under 0.2 seconds —a 10-billion-fold acceleration over older methods. This breakthrough gives coastal residents clear, instantaneous evacuation instructions, fundamentally shifting how humanity survives natural disasters.
Designing Lifesaving Drugs in Days
Developing a new medicine traditionally takes a decade of slow laboratory trial-and-error. When a new virus or treatment-resistant superbug emerges, society cannot afford to wait.
El Capitan—along with its unclassified, open-science companion system, Tuolumne— uses advanced AI agents to reinvent medicine . Instead of guessing which chemical structures might neutralize a pathogen, researchers simulate structural biology at an atomic level and screen billions of molecular compounds simultaneously. This allows scientists to design safe, targeted therapeutics in days rather than years, turning medicine into a proactive shield against future health crises.
Unleashing Unlimited Clean Energy
In late 2022, LLNL’s National Ignition Facility achieved fusion ignition, proving we could recreate the power of the sun in a lab. To turn this into a clean, limitless source of electricity for your home, commercial reactors must repeat this process multiple times every second.
El Capitan acts as the engineering bridge to a zero-carbon grid. It runs the largest fluid dynamics simulations in history to map out how burning plasma behaves under extreme pressure. By solving these complex engineering bottlenecks, the system accelerates the arrival of safe, limitless fusion energy to replace fossil fuels.
Inside the Machine: The Hardware Driving the Breakthroughs
To deliver these life-changing results, El Capitan broke records on the global High-Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark, achieving a verified 1.809 exaFLOPs of sustained performance. Built through a multi-year partnership between Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory , HPE and AMD, the machine represents a radical shift in computer architecture.
Unified Architecture: AMD Instinct™ MI300A APUs
Traditional supercomputers can spend valuable time moving data back and forth between separate CPUs and GPUs across slow internal buses. El Capitan reduces this bottleneck using AMD Instinct MI300A Accelerated Processing Units (APUs).
AMD’s architecture unifies Zen 4 CPU cores, CDNA 3 GPU cores, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) onto a single, 3D-chiplet silicon package. This shared memory space allows the chips to execute intense physics simulations and massive AI training loops simultaneously without wasting clock cycles.
Liquid Cooling and the Green500 Metrics
As scientific workloads grow, raw speed is no longer the only metric that matters; energy consumption is shaping how future leadership systems are built. Within the HPE Cray Supercomputing framework, El Capitan uses direct liquid-cooling.
A dual-loop system circulates treated water directly over the hottest components, pulling heat away far more efficiently than air. This extreme engineering delivers stunning environmental efficiency:
The efficiency metric: El Capitan achieves an energy efficiency score of 60.94 gigaFLOPs per watt.
The Green500 standing: This places the massive system at No. 28 on the Green500 list.
Securing a top efficiency rank is a great achievement for a leadership-class supercomputer, as massive systems typically face steep scaling penalties that degrade their power-to-performance ratio. El Capitan demonstrates that it is entirely possible to capture the industry-leading performance with an energy-conscious design.
Connecting the thousands of individual computing nodes is the HPE Slingshot network. This high-speed interconnect allows data to move between nodes with ultra-low latency. Furthermore, “Rabbit” near-node local storage modules stream data directly to the AMD processors, preventing data traffic jams and keeping the supercomputer running at maximum velocity.
The New Dawn of Computational Science
El Capitan serves a vital national security role in safeguarding the United States nuclear deterrent without underground testing. However, its ultimate legacy is much broader. By combining exascale raw power with generative AI, LLNL, HPE, and AMD have built a predictive engine that helps guard our coastlines, speed up medical cures, and pave the way toward clean energy. To learn more, visit hpc.llnl.gov/ .

Cyrusher's Hurricane Aimed To Be THE Full-Suspension Carbon Fiber E-Bike at $4,800 – Has No Reviews
15 photos
Photo: Cyrusher
Ever since 2014, then name Cyrusher has been a presence on the international e-bike scene, and while this team has been around for over a decade, there are still some rides in their lineup that no one has anything to say about. The most important is the Hurricane, this brand’s top-shelf machine, a fat tire e-bike completed with a carbon fiber frame.
I know, a carbon fiber frame and fat tires are probably the last thing you thought you’d ever want coming out of the e-bike industry, and frankly, I completely understand your perspective . I mean, what an out-of-the-ordinary machine, one that very few cyclists would even ride, and if they did, it’d be out of pure curiosity.
For example, the Hurricane, has been around since late 2023, and ever since then, there has been no reviews on this ride, be they written or video. The only source of information as to what this beast has to offer is what is provided by the manufacturer.
Photo: Cyrusher This can mean that no one has stepped up to the Hurricane plate, nor has Cyrusher sent any of these to influencers to shed some much-needed light onto the model, and there may be a very clear reason why: price.
According to Cyrusher’s website, the Hurricane is currently being sold for $4,800 (€4,300), a price that is sure to have countless riders looking elsewhere. I mean, even as a cyclist, I look at this sort of price tag with skepticism, knowing that for a dash under $5K, I can get my hands on a bike from a brand with decades of cycling heritage. Oh, and that’s a price tag that’s down from $6,000.
What I wasn’t able to find out was what sort of carbon fiber is used to give life to this one - Cyrusher makes no mention of this - but they do shed a ton of light on the presence of a four-bar linkage for the rear suspension with a shock mounted into the top tube, similar to XC (cross-country) MTBs.
Yes, it’s a soft-tail e-bike and despite the use of composite to give rise to the frame, once it’s all said and done, this one weighs 40.6 kg, or nearly 89.5 lbs. I'm starting to ask myself whether or not anyone would actually drop this much cash on an e-bike made from carbon fiber that weighs as much as one from aluminum. I urge you to ask yourself the same.
Photo: Cyrusher More softness is also found at the front of the ride in the form of an inverted fork with a wild 160 mm of travel as much as we find on some DH bikes, even though the Hurricane doesn’t inspire DH-worthy use. There’s no mention of rear-wheel travel, but there is a mention of a dropper post.
Another source of bump-damping abilities are the tires, especially since fats, and more so since they’re ultra fat tires. At the front and rear tires with 4.8 inches of cross-sections sit on 26-inch rims. Fat tires are also great at helping us make it through various terrains and seasons. Larger contact patches mean coasting over sand and snow too.
Being electric will also help you break away from the tarmac and riding through sand and snow, and all that power comes from a mid-mounted motor with a 1,000 W output; it’s not clear if this is a peak or nominal power. What is clear is that Bafang is the brand behind the power, a respected budget option for e-bike motors with a solid history.
Photo: Cyrusher What is mentioned is that 160 Nm (118 lb-ft) of torque will be driving the rear wheel, granting us ample power to get the whole thing moving, including a rider and cargo. Payload capacity tops out at 220 kg (485 lbs), so it’s clearly a burly carbon fiber frame, one ready for extra bits like frame bags, fork cargo mounts, and even a trailer.
The entire ecosystem is also built around a 52 V, so power delivery is higher than what other monsters of this kind offer – most operate at 48 V – and once coupled with a 20 Ah battery, we’re looking at a ride time of up 90 km (56 miles) on a full charge. Just keep in mind that this number is from a Hurricane that is limited to 25 kph (15.5 mph), according to the manufacturer’s website.
However, it can be unlocked , depending on where you are in the world, to as much as 28 mph, and since Cyrusher mentions that it classifies as a Class 3 e-bike, we can also expect throttle functionality, even though it’s not specified on the product page. The clip below does showcase a thumb throttle on the Hurricane, so we can look forward to one. Motor response is signaled by a torque sensor.
Photo: Cyrusher The rest of the Hurricane is completed by a solid four-piston, hydraulic brake setup for each wheel with motor cut-off, and a budget Shimano drivetrain.
But the question still remains whether or not this one is worth the bucks, and seeing as how there are no reviews for this ride, it's a bit difficult to say so. Then again, maybe things are more obvious than they seem, “ahem.”
